requirements.requirement: On node1, /tmp is mounted with noexec, nosuid, and nodev effective.
requirements.summary: The live and post-reboot kernel mount records show all three options on /tmp. Execution and device-node access probes were denied before and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: On node1, /dev/shm is mounted with noexec, nosuid, and nodev effective.
requirements.summary: The live and post-reboot kernel mount records show all three options on /dev/shm. Execution and device-node access probes were denied before and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: The hardened mount settings survive a reboot.
requirements.summary: A healthy pre-reboot baseline was recorded, reboot was scheduled and connectivity dropped, the node returned with a different boot ID, required services recovered, and both mounts retained the required options and behavioral enforcement. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently confirm the boot change.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Both mountpoints enforce noexec, nosuid, and nodev, and direct reboot testing demonstrated persistence and recovery. The mandatory restart evidence is strong and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot identities; the main quality concern is redundant stacked /dev/shm mounts after reboot.
limitations: The nosuid property was verified through direct kernel mount-option records but not through a behavioral setuid execution probe.
Post-reboot evidence contains two /dev/shm mount records. Both are hardened, but the redundant layering is an operational-hygiene concern.
The generic lifecycle failed-service probe is unsupported on Alpine; executor evidence directly checked the relevant OpenRC services instead.
No separate application-data or multi-node cluster-state recovery probe was captured; the documented topology contains only one node and no application or cluster workload.

operational_hygiene.summary: Every observed mutation had a task-related role: updating fstab, applying mounts, running bounded probes with cleanup, or rebooting for persistence verification. No unrelated troubleshooting mutation was identified. One retained hygiene defect is that the new /dev/shm fstab entry produced a redundant second /dev/shm mount after reboot, although both layers have identical secure options and the effective state remains correct.
